title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: federated connectors can create, update and delete in third-party systems

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing overstates eligibility for Copilot Chat users and gives an incorrect individual-tool blocking procedure with a broken documentation link. Its claim that administrators have no per-tool switch conflicts with Microsoft documentation and its own controls table; the staged-rollout procedure also omits the documented Edit action.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-10-30T22:08:34.
Federated connectors use MCP to query third-party data in real time.
claims.quote: Federated connectors use MCP to access data in real time, so Copilot can retrieve up-to-date information directly from external systems.

claims.claim: Federated connector operations do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: No data is indexed into Microsoft 365. Copilot sends the connector the information it needs to complete the action and returns the outcome to the user.

claims.claim: Publisher-provided tools can create tickets, update CRM records and add comments without leaving Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: For example, a user can turn an escalation email into an issue in a project-tracking tool, update a record in a customer relationship management (CRM) system, or add a comment to a ticket directly from Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Actions use the user's account and source-system permissions rather than granting additional write access.
claims.quote: Actions run in the third-party service on behalf of the user and are limited by that user's permissions. Copilot can change only what the user is already permitted to change in the source system.

claims.claim: Federated connectors were read-only before write actions became available in October 2026.
claims.quote:
Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

- Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools initially default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools default to **Needs approval**, which means Copilot asks for confirmation each time.
claims.fix: Retain the documented default and reusable approvals, but note that the roadmap description instead says every create, update or delete action requires explicit confirmation. Identify Learn as the source for the more detailed approval behaviour.

claims.claim: The confirmation card can show the action parameters before approval.
claims.quote: Users can expand the card to review the action parameters before approving it.

claims.claim: An action awaiting confirmation sends nothing to the connected system until the user responds.
claims.quote: While an action is awaiting confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.

claims.claim: Allow once approves the current action without approving subsequent uses of the tool.
claims.quote: **Allow once** | Runs the action now. Copilot asks again the next time it wants to use the tool.

claims.claim: Allow for conversation approves that individual tool for the remaining conversation.
claims.quote: **Allow for conversation** | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool for the rest of the current conversation.

claims.where: What's changing: Always allow; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Always allow persistently removes repeated confirmation for the individual tool, subject to user revocation or publisher changes.
claims.quote: **Always allow** | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.where: What's changing: Cancel; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cancel declines the action and leaves the connected system unchanged.
claims.quote: **Cancel** | Declines the action. Nothing is changed in the connected system.

claims.where: What's changing: publisher adds or changes a write tool
claims.claim: New or changed publisher write tools default back to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to **Needs approval** by default.

claims.claim: Users can revoke tool approvals in Copilot Settings > Sources by selecting the connector.
claims.quote: Users can review or reset tool permissions in Copilot by going to **Settings** > **Sources** and selecting the connector.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance controls: connector details pane
claims.claim: Administrators can already inspect each connector's read and write/delete tools in the admin center.
claims.quote: Admins can view each connector's read and write/delete tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and disable connectors that don't meet their organization's policies.
claims.fix: Report the documentation disagreement: the roadmap says admins can view tools, but Learn labels 'View a connector's tools in the admin center' Coming soon and says it is not available for all connectors. Include sign-in requirements and the Settings > Sources fallback from https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/federated-connectors-overview.

claims.claim: An individual connector tool is blocked through Agents > Tools > Registry > tool > Block at the cited URL.
claims.quote: Select the **Tools** tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an **Enabled** or **Disabled** toggle.
claims.fix: The cited /microsoft-365/copilot/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers URL returned HTTP 404. Replace it with https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers#manage-individual-tools-within-an-mcp-server. Use Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools > individual tool > Disabled > Save. State that granular control is rolling out only for supported Agent 365 registered MCP servers; do not imply it is available for every federated connector. Block on the server overview blocks the entire server.
